newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees Port Kembla output above 5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees Port Kembla output above 5 mln T.

text.p: Australian steel-maker, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Monday, said annual output at its Port Kembla works could well exceed five million tonnes in five years.
"I think it will be larger than five million tonnes in five years time, perhaps considerably larger," BHP managing director John Prescott told a briefing seminar.

BHP, which recently announced plans to close its Newcastle steelworks in 1999 and to keep its Port Kembla and Whyalla plants open, reported raw steel production of 4.67 million tonnes for the year to May 31, 1997.
Last Friday, BHP announced a 1996/97 (June-May) net profit of A$410 million, 60.8 percent lower than the year-ago level after abnormal writedowns of A$976 million.

It said the abnormal losses included a write-down in some North American copper assets of A$550 million, a writedown in steel assets of A$220 million and a writedown in minerals assets of A$189 million.
